title: ci(docs): gate that apps/docs/redirects.mjs destinations resolve, with all three limbs observed failing
body:
Fixes #9014

`apps/docs/redirects.mjs` is a 92-entry table of permanent (308) redirects and nothing in the repo read it. Re-measured on this branch's base (`6468df115`), both of the card's numbers still hold:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs apps/docs/redirects.mjs` printed *"No check family names the given paths in its own source"*, over **99** discovered families (the card said 98 — the farm grew).
- `git grep -l 'redirects.mjs' -- scripts .github` had **0** hits.
- The table has **92** entries today (89 page destinations + 3 wildcard destinations), so the card's count survived `62b2655d8`'s rewrite of three entries.

After this PR the same two commands report `pnpm check:docs-redirects  [lint.yml]  matched via apps/docs/redirects.mjs` and 2 hits.

## What ships

`scripts/check-docs-redirects.mjs` (dependency-free, pure filesystem, no install step, no network), `check:docs-redirects` in the root `package.json`, and one step in `lint.yml`. Three assertions:

1. **Destinations resolve the way Fumadocs routes them.** `apps/docs/lib/source.ts` is `loader({ baseUrl: '/docs' })` over `content/docs`, so `/docs/x` is served by `x.mdx`, `x.md`, `x/index.mdx` or `x/index.md`, and bare `/docs` by `index.mdx`. A destination outside the `/docs` route space is reported as UNRESOLVABLE rather than passed over — an entry this gate cannot see must not be counted in its green.
2. **Wildcard destinations resolve to a real directory.** `/docs/kernel/runtime-services/:path*` names no single page; what can be asserted is that the directory the rewritten path lands in exists.
3. **No chains**, following Next's own matching semantics: `'/a/:path*'` matches `/a` **and** `/a/deep/path`, `:path+` needs at least one segment, exact sources match exactly, first match wins. A source this gate cannot compile (an inline regex, a literal+parameter segment) is reported UNSUPPORTED rather than read as literal text — a matcher that silently stops matching is the defect being fixed, relocated into the gate.

## Proof that it can fail — the part the card said decides whether this is worth landing

**The real red → green transition, from history rather than construction.** The finished script, run unchanged against both revisions in a detached worktree:

| revision | verdict | entries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `62b2655d8^` (pre-#8948 repair) | **3 DEAD, exit 1** | 92 |
| `62b2655d8` (the repair) | **OK, exit 0** | 92 |

The three it named at `62b2655d8^` are exactly the #8948 entries — `/docs/ui/role-based-interfaces`, `/docs/ai/chatbot-integration`, `/docs/deployment/cloud-artifact-api` — at entries 45, 58 and 77. Same script, same content tree (`git diff --diff-filter=DR 62b2655d8^ HEAD -- content/docs` is empty, so no page appeared or vanished to do the work).

**The chain limb, fired against real data.** The card noted this limb had never fired outside a hand test. Pointing entry 56 at `/docs/guides/skills` — a URL that is itself the source at entry 57 — on the live table produced `1 DEAD, 1 CHAIN`, exit 1, with the chain attributed to entry 57. Reverted; `cmp` against a pre-ablation copy confirms the restored file is byte-identical and the gate is green again.

**`--self-test`, following the `check-nul-bytes.mjs` / `check-role-word.mjs` pattern** — 48 assertions over a temp fixture, running the real `loadTable` + `checkTable` path (the module import included, so the loader is exercised rather than bypassed). Two tables over one fixture content tree:

- a **clean** table carrying every resolution shape (`.mdx`, `.md`, `dir/index.mdx`, `dir/index.md`, bare `/docs`, a `#fragment`, a `?query`, a wildcard) reports **zero** findings — without this, a checker that flagged everything would pass every red fixture below;
- a **dirty** table asserted by its **exact** 10-finding set, so an over-eager checker fails as loudly as a blind one. It contains one control per limb, including the two that separate a real resolver from a lazy one: a destination pointing at a directory that **exists but has no index page** (a directory-existence check would pass it), and a wildcard destination whose prefix exists as a **file**;
- the chain controls cover all three shapes: an exact source, a `:path*` source catching a deep URL, a `:path*` source catching the **bare** URL (zero segments — the likeliest chain, and the one a naive matcher misses), and a `:path+` source reachable only by the deep probe;
- the loader refuses an empty table, a missing export and a malformed entry, so the gate cannot report OK over nothing.

Worth recording: the first draft of the dirty fixture accidentally contained two chains I had not intended, and the checker reported them. The fixture was wrong and the gate was right — that is the cheapest evidence in the file that the chain limb is not decorative, so it is noted in a comment there.

## Lane: the card's recommendation is right, its job is not

Verified against both workflow files rather than taken on trust.

**`check-links.yml` is confirmed unsuitable, and the load-bearing half of the argument holds.** Its `on:` block is exactly `workflow_dispatch` + `pull_request` — **no `merge_group`** — and its own header states this is deliberate and that promoting it without adding `merge_group` in the same change stalls the queue. A gate landed there would not block, which is the point of the card.

**But the step goes in `lint.yml`'s `ESLint` job, not its `TypeScript Type Check` job.** The required/advisory half of the card's reasoning is unaffected: `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` in `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` enrolls **both** jobs, and `lint.yml` carries `merge_group`, so either job blocks. The card's stated reason for picking `TypeScript Type Check` — *"where the other `check:*` families live"* — is the part that does not survive checking: the same ledger records the **ESLint** job as carrying *"the whole `check:*` gate family (25 steps)"*, and every docs guard sits in it (`check:doc-anchors`, `check:docs-audit-scope`, `check:role-word`, `check:quick-reference-counts`, `check:doc-authoring`). The typecheck job additionally runs a full workspace build that a dependency-free filesystem check has no use for. Placed next to `check:doc-anchors`, whose header already reasons about this exact lychee blind spot.

## Verification

Union re-derived from the final diff — `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs .github/workflows/lint.yml package.json scripts/check-docs-redirects.mjs` — and run at `58b0b9d97`, which is the head commit:

```
check:docs-redirects               PASS   (48 self-test assertions; 92 entries, 98 chain probes)
check:node-version                 PASS
check:required-contexts            PASS
check:shard-attestation            PASS
check:workflow-status-functions    PASS
check:nul-bytes                    PASS   (5953 files)
check:type-check-coverage          PASS
pnpm exec eslint scripts/check-docs-redirects.mjs   PASS
```

`check:type-check-debt` was named by the derivation and is **not** run here, stated rather than glossed. The coupling is real, not a heuristic artifact: `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`'s `observed()` genuinely reads `turbo.json`, `.github/workflows/lint.yml` and the root `package.json` — two of the three files this PR edits — to assert the workflow still invokes `typecheck:root` and `turbo run typecheck`. That half ran green above, over the edited `lint.yml` and `package.json`, as `check:type-check-coverage`. What `check:type-check-debt` adds on top is `--re-measure`, which re-runs tsc per DEBT / TEST_DEBT ledger entry and refuses outright on an unbuilt closure by design. This diff contains no TypeScript, no tsconfig and no test file, so no ledger number can move; building the full workspace closure would consume the shared verification lock for minutes to confirm numbers this diff cannot reach. It runs unconditionally in CI on this PR either way.

No changeset: the diff is `scripts/`, `.github/` and one root `package.json` script line, none of it published package source. `skip-changeset` applied.
